definition: In artificial intelligence, an embodied agent, also sometimes referred to as an interface agent, is an intelligent agent that interacts with the environment through a physical body within that environment.
details: Agents that are represented graphically with a body, for example a human or a cartoon animal, are also called embodied agents, although they have only virtual, not physical, embodiment. A branch of artificial intelligence focuses on empowering such agents to interact autonomously with human beings and the environment. Mobile robots are one example of physically embodied agents; Ananova and Microsoft Agent are examples of graphically embodied agents. Embodied conversational agents are embodied agents (usually with a graphical front-end as opposed to a robotic body) that are capable of engaging in conversation with one another and with humans employing the same verbal and nonverbal means that humans do (such as gesture, facial expression, and so forth).

explainer.lead: An embodied agent is an intelligent agent whose interaction with an environment happens through a body, either physical or graphical. The idea connects intelligent behaviour with how an agent appears, moves, gestures, or acts, rather than treating it as disembodied software.

tiers.eli5: Imagine the difference between a voice answering questions and a robot or cartoon character that can act or gesture while responding. An embodied agent is like that robot or character: its body is part of how it deals with people and its surroundings, even when the body exists only on a screen.
tiers.practitioner: Embodied agents appear in mobile robots and in graphical systems such as Ananova and Microsoft Agent. Embodied conversational agents usually use a graphical front-end and combine conversation with human-like verbal and nonverbal behaviour, including gestures and facial expressions; keep virtual embodiment distinct from physical robotic embodiment when defining system requirements.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, an embodied agent is an intelligent agent A that interacts with an environment E through a body B situated within E. The term also covers agents with graphical rather than physical bodies, while embodied conversational agents add human-like verbal and nonverbal communication; this breadth means embodiment alone does not specify a particular architecture or capability.

explainer.example: A mobile robot is a physically embodied agent because its body is located in the environment and provides the means by which it interacts there. By contrast, Microsoft Agent illustrates the graphical case: the represented body is virtual rather than physical.

usedIn.name: Mobile robots

usedIn.name: Ananova
usedIn.detail: An example of an agent embodied through a graphical representation rather than a physical body.

usedIn.name: Microsoft Agent
usedIn.detail: Another example of graphical embodiment for an intelligent agent.

usedIn.name: Embodied conversational agents
usedIn.detail: Agents, usually with graphical front-ends, that converse with people or one another using verbal and nonverbal behaviour.

explainer.intuition: Give an intelligent agent a body and its interaction with the world can happen through that body. The body may be a mobile robot in a physical environment or a human or cartoon figure in a graphical interface.
howItWorks: Start with an intelligent agent that needs to interact with people, other agents, or its environment.
Give it a physical body situated in that environment, or represent it graphically with a virtual body.
Use that body as the means through which the agent interacts with its surroundings.
For conversational agents, usually provide a graphical front-end and support verbal and nonverbal communication such as gestures and facial expressions.
explainer.whyItMatters: Embodiment provides a common way to think about intelligent behaviour in robots and graphically represented agents. It also supports autonomous interaction with people and the environment, including communication through both words and human-like nonverbal signals.
misconceptions: An embodied agent need not have a physical body; graphical human or cartoon representations also count as virtual embodiment.
Embodied conversational agents are not necessarily robots and usually have graphical front-ends.
Embodiment is not a single algorithm or architecture; it describes how an agent is situated and interacts.
